question: Should ClawHub expose claimState, officialState, and restrictionState on the admin official-publisher list now, and should saturated membership buckets ever produce claimed without observing an active user?
rationale: This PR changes a trust-state API vocabulary that affects publisher identity interpretation, and source review cannot choose the product/security semantics on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Accept after fixing derivation and proof
options.body: Expose the state object only after claimed requires an observed active linked/member user and the contributor posts redacted runtime/API proof.

options.title: Split spec from API field
options.body: Land or revise the internal spec first and defer the admin response field until the trust-state vocabulary is settled.

options.title: Defer to the claim-policy RFC
options.body: Keep this draft paused until https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/issues/2320 has a maintainer synthesis for claim and inactive-owner semantics.

recommendation.title: Accept after fixing derivation and proof
recommendation.body: Expose the state object only after claimed requires an observed active linked/member user and the contributor posts redacted runtime/API proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen owns the most relevant official-publisher admin API history and authored the overlapping claim/recovery RFC.
